children: It was appropriate for the Bank of Japan to continue raising interest rates and adjust the degree of monetary accommodation in response to developments in the economy, prices, and financial conditions, according to its September meeting minutes.

Members agreed that the timing and pace of further adjustments should be determined by assessing the likelihood of achieving the central bank’s baseline economic and inflation outlook, while monitoring risks such as the impact of the situation in the Middle East, expanding AI-related demand, and forex movements.
They also stressed the growing importance of stabilising underlying CPI inflation around the 2% target to prevent an upward deviation that could hurt the economy.

One member noted that monetary policy had entered a new phase, shifting from encouraging higher underlying inflation toward ensuring price stability through flexible responses to domestic and overseas economic developments, including exchange-rate-driven price pressures.

title: BoJ Sees Case for Further Rate Hikes: September Minutes
